Subject: Encryption & KMS options — follow up from today's call

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo and the clear overview today. Quick recap from our side and a few follow-ups so we can align with security/compliance: 

- Data scope: PII will be sent to Redwood primarily as user identifiers and form submissions across a set of API routes (login, KYC upload).
- Residency: we need storage and processing to remain in US-only regions (no EU/APAC storage for this data).
- Retention: our policy is 7 years for transactional records, but we can discuss shorter retention for derived artifacts.
- Logging: we need audit logging for model access and admin operations. Logs containing PII must be redacted or excluded from analytics.
- Encryption: must be TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest. Preferred: customer-managed keys (KMS/CMEK) and HSM option for root keys.

Can you confirm which of these Redwood supports on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments, and what the operational uplift would be (latency / cost) if we opt for CMEK or HSM? Also, can you share your SOC2 summary and any KMS integration docs we can circulate to our security team?

If helpful, Leah (cc'd) will collect our security questionnaire responses and hop on a technical call next week.

Thanks,
Samir

Hi Samir / Leah,

Good to chat — thanks for summarizing. High-level answers inline below, then proposed next steps.

Recap / short answers:
- In-transit: Redwood enforces TLS 1.2+ by default; mutual TLS (mTLS) is available for Dedicated and Private deployments.
- At-rest: All persisted data is encrypted with AES-256. We use envelope encryption; at-rest keys are wrapped with a root key.
- Customer-managed keys (CMEK): Supported on Hosted via AWS KMS/GCP CMEK with envelope encryption; customer controls the root key via the cloud KMS. Private and Dedicated offer stronger isolation and can be configured with BYOK/HSM.
- HSM support: Available for Private deployments (FIPS-validated HSMs) and via partner HSM integrations for Dedicated (bring-your-own-HSM on request).
- Logging & retention: Audit logs (access, admin operations) are retained by default for 90 days. We can extend retention and configure PII redaction filters for logs on Dedicated/Private tiers. Hosted customers can request extended retention as an add-on.

Attachments: I've attached our SOC 2 Type 2 summary and our encryption whitepaper which has an architecture diagram and example CMEK config.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Technical deep-dive with our infra team to walk CMEK/HSM config and network requirements (I’ve put Dev on copy).
2) Share your threat model / questionnaire items before the call so we can prep answers and configs.
3) I'll ask Commercial to prepare a scoped uplift estimate for CMEK/HSM (Aditya will take point).

Availability: Dev and I are available Tues/Wed next week in the afternoon PST. What works for your security team?

Best,

Hi Samir / Leah — following up with some technical clarifications so the deep-dive is efficient.

1) CMEK model (hosted):
- We perform envelope encryption. Customer key (CMK) in AWS KMS / GCP CMEK wraps the data-encryption-keys (DEKs). Redwood does not persist the CMK; only the wrapped DEKs are stored by the service.
- Key rotation: KMS-managed rotation supported. Rotations are seamless for DEKs; we recommend rotation cadence aligned to your policy (e.g., 90 days).

2) HSM / BYOK (Private / Dedicated):
- Private deployment: root keys may reside in a customer-controlled HSM (FIPS 140-2/140-3). We support PKCS#11 and cloud-HSM integrations; Redwood never has plaintext access to root material.
- Dedicated: we can enable a tenant-specific KMS proxy and integrate with customer HSMs; some network config (VPC peering / private link) is required.

3) Logging and PII handling:
- Application logs exclude request bodies by default; access logs contain request metadata (timestamp, route, model ID, request size). PII redaction filters can be configured to mask specific fields before logs are persisted to analytics or exported.
- Audit logs (admin/action) are tamper-evident and can be forwarded to your SIEM via secure delivery.

4) Performance / cost uplift:
- CMEK: negligible latency impact for typical API calls (single additional KMS call per DEK rotation; DEKs cached). Cost uplift depends on cloud KMS request volume; typically low for tokenized LLM workloads.
- HSM-backed root keys (BYOK): small additional latency at key unwrap times during DEK rotation but minimal at token-level runtime. Pricing uplift estimate we will provide (commercial).

Please send your security questionnaire and any network egress/inbound rules up front. For the deep-dive, we'll bring a short demo of CMEK key rotation and a sample PKCS#11 integration doc.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
